clue.text: Certainly a lowish bid by girl

parts.note: one no-trump, written 1NT, is a low opening bid in bridge, with I standing for one
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a girl's bid at the bridge table was, certainly, on the low side.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, one no-trump is a modest opening bid, written 1NT; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are adverbial assurances that a statement is genuinely so, used interchangeably for emphasis.

clue.text: Girl hangs onto old recipe for a key material

indicators.note: to hang onto something is to hold it, so the outer name wraps round what it grips

parts.note: a girl's name
standard abbreviation for old
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin 'take' on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A girl clings to an old recipe that calls for some key ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: IVY holds O and R. The 'key material' is literal: piano keys were traditionally faced with IVORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant tusk was the traditional facing for the white notes on a piano keyboard.

clue.text: Rave tribe ask about Ecstasy sudden deaths

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed round another
to rave is to rant wildly, so the letters lose their sober order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A raving tribe of clubbers asks around for Ecstasy, with sudden deaths as the grim outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sudden deaths' looks like a tabloid drug story, but it is the sporting sense: extra play to settle a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, sudden death is a playoff format where the first score wins, used to break level scores.

clue.text: Perhaps loosen carpet round top of stairs and take pile down

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a carpet is held down by tacks, so loosening it is one way to remove them

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of stairs

explanation.surface: A household job: lift the stair carpet from the top landing, then carry a heap of stuff downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags that UNTACK is only one way to loosen a carpet. 'Pile' suggests carpet pile but means a stack.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a heap of things piece by piece is to undo how they were stacked.

clue.text: A bed scattered with stash around its top part

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a stash is a hidden store, a hoard

indicators.note: things scattered are thrown about out of their order

parts.note: the letters to be scattered

explanation.surface: A bed is strewn with someone's secret stash, hidden around the upper end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' refers back to the bed in the surface: the definition is the top part of a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright panel at the pillow end of a bed frame is its uppermost structural piece.

clue.text: Undamaged monitor about to be sent back inside

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a school monitor is a prefect; its RE is the part to be turned

indicators.note: something sent back travels the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A screen arrives unbroken, yet it is about to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: PREFECT already holds RE; turning that RE round inside the word converts PREFECT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without flaw or damage is in flawless condition, as unblemished as when made.

clue.text: Serenity's heard — Moonlight Sonata perhaps

indicators.note: what is heard is sound alone, so spelling can change

parts.note: serenity is calm, a word that sounds identical

explanation.surface: A listener says Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata sounds like pure serenity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the sonata as one example of the answer, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's sonata is one example of a musical composition, which musicians call a work or item.

clue.text: Swine from E Devon waterway?

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
the Otter is the river that runs through East Devon

explanation.surface: A pig apparently escaped from a river in east Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Otter is a river in East Devon, south-west England; R is the map abbreviation for river.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a swine means they are a contemptible scoundrel, an old-fashioned insult.

clue.text: Strain of electronic glam rock band turned up

parts.note: standard abbreviation for electronic

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: T. Rex was a 1970s British glam rock band

explanation.surface: A strain of electronic music from a glam rock band gets the volume turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' sounds like volume, but in a down clue it means the band's name reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to strain is to make a great effort, to apply force or energy.

clue.text: Initially cornered 25 5D in Kafka's work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the chess piece that begins the game in a corner square
second meaning: Franz Kafka's unfinished novel

explanation.surface: A chess piece is somehow trapped inside one of Kafka's novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 and 5D combine to give a chess piece; the rook, also called a castle, starts the game on a corner square.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is commonly called a castle and starts in the board's corners; Kafka's novel Das Schloss is known in English by that title.

clue.text: The main writers in Donegal oddly unrepresented

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece goes inside the other
leaving the odd-numbered letters out keeps only the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters, once D, N, G and L are dropped
pens are writing implements

explanation.surface: Leading authors from County Donegal are strangely absent from some list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' looks like 'the principal', but it is the old poetic word for the sea. Donegal is a county in north-west Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry 'the main' means the ocean, the wide expanse of water away from any coast.

clue.text: Master enters Exeter prepared for highest degree

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece sits within the other
something prepared has been worked into a new form

parts.note: the city's letters are to be rearranged
M is the abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A Master's student arrives at Exeter University ready to study for the top degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' and 'highest degree' suggest academia; here the degree is one of extent, not a qualification. Exeter is a university city in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: The utmost point on a scale is reached when something goes as far as it possibly can.

clue.text: Mashed barley left out as herbal drink

indicators.note: mashed food is crushed out of its original shape
something out has been taken away

parts.note: the grain's letters to be worked on
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Barley is mashed, but left aside rather than used as a herbal infusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mashed barley' suggests brewing, but barley loses its L and the rest is reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerba maté is a South American infusion brewed from holly leaves, often just called by its first word.

clue.text: A long note to inspire read out by Winstone

indicators.note: spoken by a Cockney actor, so the word is said with a London accent

parts.note: to inspire is to breathe in, and a Cockney says the TH as V

explanation.surface: Ray Winstone gives a lengthy memo meant to motivate the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray Winstone is an English actor with a strong Cockney accent, in which TH often becomes V, so 'breathe' comes out with a V.
explanation.definitionFit: In music notation the breve is a note lasting twice a whole note, the longest in common use.

clue.text: Drink to consume when cycling

indicators.note: cycling goes round and round, so letters move from one end to the other

parts.note: to consume food is to eat

explanation.surface: Advice to take a drink while out riding a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the last letter of EAT to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot beverage brewed from leaves is a standard example of something to drink.

clue.text: Maybe thiamine deficiency is dismal

parts.note: thiamine is vitamin B1, one example of a B vitamin
a deficiency is a lack

explanation.surface: A medical verdict: being short of thiamine is a miserable condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags thiamine as one example of a B vitamin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloomy, hopeless outlook is often described as dark or bleak, as in a black mood.

clue.text: Richer gambler on his way

parts.note: one who bets
someone off is departing, on their way

explanation.surface: A gambler walks away from the table with more money than he came with.
explanation.walkthrough: BETTER here is one who bets, not the comparative of good.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a more comfortable financial position is the idiomatic meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: It's found in coal gas and seaweed

indicators.note: something found in a phrase is sitting inside its letters

parts.note: spans the join between the two words

explanation.surface: A chemistry quiz: name something present in both coal gas and seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seaweed' looks like a second place to search, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweeds are marine algae, so a single seaweed plant is one of them.

clue.text: Metal worker to work with large medal hit when cast

parts.note: a machine that works is said to go

indicators.note: casting metal reshapes it in a mould, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large
the Distinguished Service Medal
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A metalworker labours over a large medal, striking it as it is cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medal hit' looks like one anagram fodder, but the medal is DSM and only 'hit' is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes jewellery and objects from a precious yellow metal is a specific kind of metalworker.

clue.text: Bring short strap back and wallop

indicators.note: a short word lacks its last letter
to bring something back is to return it the way it came, so read it backwards
back means in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: a tawse is a Scottish leather strap once used for punishment, cut short

explanation.surface: A call to bring back corporal punishment and give someone a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: A tawse is a leather strap formerly used in Scottish schools; the indicator 'Bring ... back' is split around the strap.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for striking something hard with a quick blow.

clue.text: Attack entrance to broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so only sound matters

parts.note: an entrance is a way in

explanation.surface: An instruction to storm the door of a radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way in to' and the answer phrase sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To set about someone vigorously, physically or verbally, is to assault or criticise them hard.

clue.text: Time to beg for a job

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to beg is to ask

explanation.surface: It is time to start pleading with someone for employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is the link, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work someone has to do is a chore or assignment.

clue.text: Said Python is a graven image

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so only the sound counts

parts.note: Eric Idle was a member of the Monty Python comedy team

explanation.surface: Someone claims a Monty Python member is a carved deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Python' suggests a snake or the language, but it is the comedy troupe, and Eric Idle is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A graven image is the biblical phrase for a carved statue worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Pasty initially expelled after a tiny bit

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the piece before it in the clue goes second

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit'

indicators.note: initially points to the start of a word, its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of expelled

explanation.surface: A pasty was thrown up right after just a small mouthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' reads as the pie, but it is the adjective for a pale complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasty complexion is pale and unhealthy-looking, drained of colour.

clue.text: Webmaster's expurgated lexicographer

indicators.note: an expurgated text has had material cut from it

parts.note: the site manager, with the MA (Master of Arts) cut out

explanation.surface: A website manager has turned censor of a dictionary-maker's words.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. MA, the master's degree, is the part removed from inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah Webster compiled the first great American dictionary, so he is a famous dictionary-maker.

clue.text: A small bloomer from soprano Miss 14A (originally Miss 21A)

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
the singer Cilla Black was born Priscilla White

explanation.surface: A small flower blooms from a soprano who changed her stage name.
explanation.walkthrough: 14A is BLACK and 21A is WHITE: Cilla Black, a British singer and TV presenter, was born Priscilla White.
explanation.definitionFit: Squills are small bulbous plants with blue flowers; the genus name serves for any one of them.

clue.text: First person to be caught in part of storm

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, so sound rather than spelling matters

parts.note: the first person pronoun is I

explanation.surface: The first to get trapped in a section of a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like a container indicator, but here it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The calm clear centre of a hurricane or cyclone is called by this name.

clue.text: Some toe the line for noble girl

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of its run of letters

parts.note: runs across the three words

explanation.surface: Some must obey the rules for the sake of an aristocratic girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The name derives from Old English for noble, which explains the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This girl's name comes from the Old English element meaning nobility, so it literally means noble.

clue.text: Parts of foot missing in second contest with men

indicators.note: something missing has gone, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a foot is twelve inches
the letters dropped
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: With some toes missing, a man struggles in his second contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts of foot' suggests toes, but the measurement is meant. 'Men' are chessmen, the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game played with pieces called chessmen is a contest using men.

clue.text: Term for structure of skeleton — a key material

indicators.note: a term is an end, so this picks the final letter

parts.note: last letter of structure
made of bone, like a skeleton

explanation.surface: A biology term for the framework of a skeleton, then a key material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' means end, as in termination. Piano black keys were traditionally made of EBONY, partnering 1D.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hardwood traditionally used for the black notes on a piano keyboard.

clue.text: One harbour in trouble without our Indian state

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray
without means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Roman numeral for one
the port word to be shortened
these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A harbour in difficulty, minus our presence, in one Indian state.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OUR from the port word leaves HARB, which joins I before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a state in eastern India, with Patna as its capital.

clue.text: Around yard stags like marshy grasses

indicators.note: turning around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yard
stags are male deer

explanation.surface: Stags gather around a yard, resembling the grasses of a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container indicator, but it turns the whole pair round.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses of wetlands, so the adjective means resembling or full of them.

clue.text: A board game and some books welcome

parts.note: the Old Testament, a group of books of the Bible
a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A board game and a few books are offered as a welcome gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some books' is OT, the Old Testament. The board game, played with black and white discs, also suits the puzzle's black-and-white theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-player strategy game of flipping black and white discs on a grid goes by this name, after Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: 9 heading off to collect 10 sons — that's 10

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so one piece holds the other
with the heading off, the opening letter is gone

parts.note: the number written as a word, losing its first letter
the number written as a word
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father of nine takes in his ten sons, a household that sounds exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 and the first 10 are plain numbers, not cross-references; only the last 10 refers to EXTREME at 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and intense both describe something felt or done to a very high degree.

clue.text: Deceptive appearances? Everyone in fancy dress disheartened

definitions.note: plural against a singular answer: each deceptive appearance is one

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle letter
in means within, so one piece goes inside the other
to dress is to clothe, wrapping something in an outer layer

parts.note: fancy with its central N removed
everyone is all

explanation.surface: At a fancy dress party nobody is what they seem, and everyone feels downhearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy dress' reads as a costume, but fancy is the fodder, losing its middle letter, and dress wraps it round everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistaken belief or misleading argument is something that seems true but deceives, so the question mark flags a loose definition.

clue.text: Good will or ill, new year follows old

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so the piece named first in the clue goes second

parts.note: ill as a noun is harm
standard abbreviation for old
standard abbreviation for new
standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Whether the coming year brings good or bad, a new one always follows the old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' places the new year after old, so O comes first. 'Good will' reads as a wish but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly agreement and peaceful relations between people are a state of mutual goodwill.
